learn-ai-fluency.title: AI Fluency Ladder
learn-ai-fluency.purpose: What good AI use looks like at ENEC: four rungs across four dimensions, with plant examples and a target for every job family.

my-ai-fluency.title: My AI fluency
my-ai-fluency.purpose: Your rung on the AI fluency ladder from your skill evidence, why, and the next step.

my-ai-fitness.title: AI and digital fitness check
my-ai-fitness.purpose: A short adaptive check of your digital and AI skills, once a quarter; the trend is yours.

workforce-ai-fluency.title: AI and digital fluency across ENEC
workforce-ai-fluency.purpose: The share of staff above basic, the fluency rungs and progress against the leadership target, suppressed under 10.

training-ai-fitness-items.title: Fitness check item bank
training-ai-fitness-items.purpose: The bilingual items behind the AI and digital fitness check, their coverage and their versions.

reason.rung: Rung {rung} of 4: every dimension is evidenced at each rung up to this one.

met.mindset: Human-centred mindset shown at rung {rung} (skill level {level}).
met.ethics: Ethics and assurance shown at rung {rung} (skill level {level}).
met.techniques: Techniques and applications shown at rung {rung} (skill level {level}).
met.design: System design shown at rung {rung} (skill level {level}).

gap.mindset: For rung {rung}: human-centred mindset needs level {level} evidence.
gap.ethics: For rung {rung}: ethics and assurance needs level {level} evidence.
gap.techniques: For rung {rung}: techniques and applications need level {level} evidence.
gap.design: For rung {rung}: system design needs level {level} evidence.

reason.engineering: {n} AI-engineering skills are shown apart and do not raise the literacy rung.

lad.intro: What good use of AI looks like in a plant where AI must be challenged, not obeyed. Four rungs, each revisiting the same four dimensions at a deeper level, with plant examples. Your rung comes from evidence, never from points.

grid.title: The ladder
grid.intro: Each cell says what the rung looks like in one dimension, an example from plant work, and the literacy skills (with the level) that evidence it.

spiral.title: Spiral progression
spiral.body: Every rung covers all four dimensions again, more deeply. You reach a rung when all four are evidenced at it and at every rung below; self-ratings alone never move you up.

tracks.title: AI literacy is not AI engineering
tracks.intro: Everyone needs AI literacy. AI engineering is a specialist track: useful, but it never raises the literacy rung.
tracks.note: An engineer who builds data pipelines still needs to show verification and judgement to climb the ladder.

how.title: How your rung is worked out
how.s1: Your skill evidence (qualifications, training, assessments, work, credentials and the fitness check) sets a level on each skill.
how.s2: Only AI-literacy skills count; self-claimed levels do not.
how.s3: A cell is met when one of its skills is at or above the cell's level.
how.s4: Your rung is the highest rung with all four dimensions met at it and below.

cta.signin: Sign in to see your rung

targets.title: Targets by job family
targets.intro: What each job family aims for, and why. Operators: Practitioner, plus the verification cell of Assurer.

noGame.title: No points, no streaks, no leaderboards
noGame.body: The ladder describes evidence. It does not rank people, award points or reward streaks, and nobody else sees your rung; leaders see only suppressed aggregates.

my.intro: Your rung on the AI fluency ladder, worked out from your skill evidence. Each reason points at the evidence behind it.
my.none: The AI fluency ladder is for ENEC staff.

hero.title: You are at
hero.zero: No dimension is evidenced at every rung yet. The fitness check is the quickest way to show where you stand.
hero.rule: Only AI-literacy evidence counts; self-ratings alone and AI-engineering skills never raise the rung.

grid.title: My ladder
grid.intro: Green cells are evidenced; the highlighted row is your next rung.

next.title: To reach {rung}
next.top: You are at the top rung
next.ready: All four dimensions are met at the next rung.
next.topBody: Keep your evidence current: it ages, and the check is quarterly.

target.title: Target for {family}
target.none: No target is set for your family.

eng.title: AI engineering skills
eng.note: These are valuable specialist skills. They are kept apart from the literacy rung on purpose.

honest.title: An honest ladder
honest.body: {max} rungs, no points and no streaks. Your rung changes only when evidence changes, and evidence ages: digital and AI skills fall in the fast-changing decay class.

fit.intro: A short adaptive check of your digital and AI skills. It takes about ten minutes, adapts to your answers and is scored on the server. You can take it once a quarter.
fit.none: The fitness check is for ENEC staff.

q.noKey: Answers are checked on the server; you see your result at the end.

start.title: About the check
start.b1: 18 to {max} items: it stops as soon as every area is settled.
start.b2: Nine areas: the five DigComp areas and the four AI dimensions. Safety and problem solving carry extra weight.
start.b3: Your result is written to your skills passport as assessment evidence, never above level {cap}. Higher levels need work evidence.
start.b4: Once a quarter. Your quarterly trend is the result that matters.
start.nextOn: You have taken this quarter's check. The next one opens on {date}.

fit.doneBody: You answered {n} items. Your result and the evidence it wrote are below.
fit.noResultBody: Take the check to see your result, the ENEC average and your family's target.

res.title: Result for {period}
res.intro: Your score with the ENEC average and your family's target as comparison lines, your profile by area and the evidence written to your skills.
res.enecSuppressed: The ENEC average appears once 10 or more people have a result.
res.noEvidence: No area reached level 1, so no evidence was written.
res.evidenceNote: This check replaces the evidence of your earlier checks; it says where you stand now.

bandText.limited: Below basic: start with the governed-use course and the Aware cells of the ladder.
bandText.basic: Basic: you know the essentials. The Practitioner cells show what to practise next.
bandText.above_basic: Above basic: you use digital and AI tools with care. Keep verifying what tools produce.
bandText.advanced: Advanced: strong across most areas. Higher rungs need evidence from real work.

trend.title: My quarterly trend
trend.one: Your trend appears after your second quarterly check.

privacy.title: Who sees this
privacy.body: Only you see your answers and score. HR sees organisation aggregates only, with any group under 10 people suppressed. The check never asks about plant security.

reason.confirmed: {area}: a confirming item settled your level (weighted area).
reason.cap: Evidence from the check is capped at level {level}; higher levels need work evidence.

wf.intro: How digital and AI fluency is spreading across ENEC staff: the DigComp-style "% above basic" indicator from the fitness check, and the fluency rungs from skill evidence. Aggregates only; cells under 10 people are suppressed.
wf.none: These aggregates are for HR analysts and the HR director.

tile.aboveSub: of {n} tested in the last four quarters

above.title: % of staff above basic
above.apart: The EU figure is a separate external benchmark line; it is not an ENEC measurement and the two are not merged.

trend.title: Quarterly trend
trend.eyebrow: Latest check per person in each quarter
trend.note: A quarter with fewer than 10 results is suppressed and shows as a gap.

areas.title: Average level by area
areas.intro: Mean level (0-3) across the latest results; weighted areas in the accent colour.

fam.title: By job family
fam.intro: Families with fewer than 10 people tested are suppressed. Security, safeguards and cyber are never broken out.

above.d: A result band of above basic or advanced (score 50 or more) on the latest check.

window.d: The latest completed check per active staff member in the quarters {window}.

prac.d: Rung 2 or higher on the AI fluency ladder, computed from skill evidence for every active staff member.

target.d: A dated target chosen by leadership for the demo, shown beside the measured value. It is not a claim about the future.

suppress.d: Any cell naming fewer than 10 people is shown as suppressed, never as a value.

restricted.d: Security, safeguards and cyber appear in totals only, never as their own rows.

noRank.title: Aggregates, not rankings
noRank.body: No individual's score or rung is shown here, and families are not ranked. Use the numbers to target learning, not to judge people.

bank.intro: The bilingual items behind the AI and digital fitness check. Training staff read the bank and its key; the training manager adds, edits and retires items. The server re-checks every rule on save.

coverage.title: Coverage by area and difficulty
coverage.eyebrow: At least {min} active items per cell
coverage.ok: Every area and difficulty has enough active items for re-takes.

rules.title: Item rules
rules.r1: A question and 3 or 4 options in English and Arabic, with one key.
rules.r2: Never about plant security: wording that touches security arrangements is refused.
rules.r3: Each area and difficulty keeps at least two active items so re-takes vary.
rules.r4: Edits raise the version; items are retired, never deleted.

bank.readonly: You can read the bank. Only the training manager edits it.

security.title: Awareness only
security.body: Cyber items cover personal hygiene (phishing, removable media, passwords) only. Plant security arrangements never appear in the bank.

problem.stem: Write the question in both languages (up to 400 characters).
problem.options: Give 3 or 4 options in both languages.
problem.correct: The correct option must be one of the options.

bank.retireBody: The item stops being served. It stays in the bank, and the server refuses if its area and difficulty would drop below two active items.
